question: Does changing only the supported per-process ATen DispatchStub capability selection change CaTiO3 observables with identical inputs, graphs, parameters and captured conditions?

hypotheses.H_control: A fresh control matches saved R1 inputs, all graph/model output arrays, parameters and ASE observations exactly.
hypotheses.H_dispatch: ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY=default changes at least one finite ASE observable under invariant input/graph/weights and otherwise equal captured effective settings.
hypotheses.H_repeat: If H_dispatch is observed, one fresh altered-condition repeat matches all altered model outputs and ASE observables exactly.

conditions.purpose: Fresh negative control vs saved R1; require all captured model and ASE outputs exact.

conditions.conditional: Only after C0 capture/integrity and exact R1 control gate pass.
Only if C1 invariants/captures pass and at least one finite ASE energy/force/stress component differs from C0 exactly.
conditions.purpose: Test repeatability of observed altered-condition response; not a spare attempt.

interpretation: C0 mismatch stops contrast: current control not identified.
Changed capability with invariant inputs/graphs/parameters and finite observable changes supports sensitivity to this per-process ATen dispatch selection in this build.
No observable change is a bounded negative result; do not spend third evaluation or try another setting.
Only model-intermediate change with equal ASE observables is internal sensitivity, not altered physical-observable evidence; no third run.
C2 exact output match supports repeatability for this pair of altered processes; mismatch stops with nonrepeatability.
Any historical-baseline threshold failures remain failed. A changed result or accidental baseline match is neither a correction nor evidence of historical host settings.
This setting does not globally disable AVX or control every MKL/oneDNN kernel. No per-kernel tracing is claimed.
invariants: Exact raw CIF/config, 20 atoms, no relaxation
All saved input and consumed neighbor arrays, all eight graph arrays exact including dtype/shape/order and data hashes
All model-parameter tensor hashes exact; same package/model/source/config hashes and dependency versions
All captured runtime settings equal except condition label, ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY and observed CPU capability
Same CPU affinity [0], seed20261024 for Python/NumPy/PyTorch and Python hash seed, all numerical-library controls and PyTorch intra-op/inter-op threads one
C0 additionally requires all six model-output arrays and ASE observables exact vs R1; C2 exact vs C1
capture_criteria: Unchanged R1-validated published recorder; exactly one graph and model call; nonempty finite input/neighbor/graph/model arrays; saved byte hashes and manifests all verify
Six expected output tensors; 20x3 forces and 3x3 stress; exact float32 model-to-ASE conversion including stress symmetrization

Record all signed differences new minus named reference, every component, shape/dtype/finite/equality/tolerance decisions against R1/C0/C1 as applicable and both historical baselines plus replay; missing D1 remains unavailable
stop_conditions: Exception, nonfinite/missing capture, timeout, integrity failure, source/model/input mismatch or broken declared comparison assumption: stop further inference and preserve all available output.
No more than three new evaluations; <=600 seconds total calculation process wall and <=1800 seconds investigation from recorded start; no retry of failed condition.
No overlap, changed ownership/public head, disallowed/unavailable included-usage gate, extra fee warning: checkpoint and defer.
Do not search alternate settings to match old baseline. Original acceptance failure alone is reported but is not a broken current contrast assumption; it is already the retained outcome.

source_support.scope: Public upstream source at installed PyTorch build commit; compiled installed binary checked separately

scope: Same cloud task; no packages changed, new environment, S1/S2/S3 campaign, publication, schedule change or fallback retirement.
